provenance.instrument: Darby Township Zoning Ordinance of 2007 (Chapter 27 Zoning, Ord. 670 of 12/12/2007, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 DA2308, Township of Darby (Delaware County Department of Public Health named in 27-204 'Public sewer'). Not Darby borough or Upper Darby. District use lists and lot, yard, coverage and height figures are text tables in Parts 4 to 9. Attachments: Appendix A, Diagrams of Requirements, and the Zoning Map (PDFs, not opened). Floodplain rules are in Chapter 8. Chapter 17 only points to Chapter 27. New Laws: Ord. No. 733 (Chapter 21) and No. 755 (Appendix D), none on zoning
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 Version Information: 'Includes legislation through 01-08-2025.' Uploaded on 09-10-2025. New Laws: two, neither amending Chapter 27
checks: The code has no accessory dwelling unit. Each residential district permits listed uses 'and no other' (27-400, 27-501, 27-601, 27-801), and the R-A accessory uses are a private garage, shed or gazebo, a no-impact home-based business and a family-based community residence facility (27-400.5, 27-400.6)

'Garages shall not be used for permanent or temporary human habitation' (27-403.3E). Garages stand only in rear yards, at least 10 ft behind the rear of the house, at most 15 ft tall, 3 ft from the rear line and 2 ft from a side line (27-403.3). One shed of at most 120 sq ft and 8 ft is allowed in the rear or side yard (27-403.1)

'In residential districts, only one principal building may be erected on each lot' (27-204 'Principal building'). A family is related persons, or up to five unrelated persons living as one housekeeping unit 'with single kitchen facilities' (27-204)

A two-family detached dwelling is permitted by right in R-B, and in R-C, which takes the R-B uses: 5,000 sq ft per two-family dwelling, 50 ft wide, front yard 30 ft, side yards 20 ft together and 8 ft each, rear 25 ft (27-501.3, 27-601.1). The code defines it as two families 'with one family living wholly or partly over the other' and no party wall (27-204). Each use list lets a building be 'erected, altered or used' for a listed use (27-400, 27-501, 27-601), and the parking rule counts uses made 'by conversion' (27-1300.3). So an existing detached house may be altered into a two-family detached dwelling by right, if one unit is wholly or partly over the other. A side-by-side addition or a separate building is not that dwelling

The A district permits only apartment buildings (12 units or more) and two-family attached dwellings, 6,000 sq ft per two-family dwelling, at most six attached (27-801). C-1 bars any residential use with its uses, and the general commercial and LI districts list no dwellings (27-901.2, 27-902, 27-1001). In LI the accessory uses include 'living quarters for watchmen', and 'No residential dwellings are permitted in the Light Industrial Districts' (27-1001.3A, 27-1001.5A)

R-D is an existing neighborhood of attached houses: 'No permanent additions or enclosed porches are permitted', 'No accessory buildings are permitted' and 'No business or accessory use is permitted' (27-701)

No use variance bar was found. The Zoning Hearing Board decides variances on the hardship findings of 27-1718. The code has no section on nonconforming lots or on adding units to a nonconforming building

Parking: 'One- and two-family dwellings: two spaces per dwelling unit' (27-1300.3M), and 'If the computation results in a fraction, a parking space shall be required for each fractional amount'. In residential districts all required parking must be behind the building line, and no vehicle may park in the front yard (27-1300.2). All parking spaces must have hard surfaces (27-1300.1D(4))

Floodplain (Chapter 8): any new construction or substantial improvement needs its lowest floor at or above the regulatory flood elevation, and basements are prohibited (8-502.1, 8-502.3A). No construction in the floodway without an analysis showing no rise and a DEP permit (8-402A). In an AE area without a floodway, nothing new within 50 ft landward of the top of bank unless DEP's regional office issues a permit (8-402B(2)(b)). Development includes the renovation, expansion or alteration of a building (8-902), so this reaches work inside a house too. An accessory structure in the floodplain 'shall not be designed or used for human habitation' and may be at most 200 sq ft, whether or not it is elevated (8-502.5A, B). Work on an existing building of 50% or more of its market value is a substantial improvement and must fully comply. Smaller work is elevated or floodproofed to the greatest extent possible (8-701, 8-702). 'Within any identified floodplain area, manufactured homes shall be prohibited', and no variance may be granted (8-506)

Stormwater (Chapter 26, Ord. No. 749): where a perennial or intermittent stream, lake, pond or wetland is on a site, a regulated activity needs a riparian buffer of at least 50 ft from the top of bank (26-223.1). On an existing lot whose rear or side setback is under 50 ft the buffer may shrink to 25% of the setback or 25 ft, whichever is greater, or further with municipal approval or waiver (26-223.2A). This is not a floodplain rule, so it reaches lots outside the mapped floodplain

term.note: Searched for in-law, accessory apartment, accessory dwelling, second dwelling, ECHO, caretaker, living quarters, guest house, garage apartment, extended family, household employee, conversion, servant and habitation, and read every district use list. No ADU use. The only hits are a janitor's living quarters in an apartment house (27-204) and living quarters for watchmen as an LI accessory use, where no dwellings are permitted (27-1001.3A, 27-1001.5A)

status.note: No district lists a second dwelling on a single-family lot. Each list permits named uses 'and no other'

status_by_form.note: 'Garages shall not be used for permanent or temporary human habitation.' Written in the R-A Part. R-B and R-C uses conform with these rules (27-501.1, 27-601.1)

path.note: A second unit on a single-family lot is not a listed use, so the path is a use variance from the Zoning Hearing Board. In R-B and R-C a detached house may be altered into a two-family detached dwelling by right (see the other paths)

fallback_path.note: Zoning Hearing Board on the hardship findings of 27-1718.1

value.name: Two-family detached dwelling, new or by altering a house (R-B, R-C)
value.conditions: Two families in one detached building 'with one family living wholly or partly over the other' and no party wall (27-204). A building may be 'erected, altered or used' for it, so an existing detached house may be altered into one (27-501, 27-601). A side-by-side addition or a second building does not fit the definition. 5,000 sq ft per two-family dwelling, 50 ft wide and 50 ft of frontage, front yard 30 ft, side yards 20 ft together and 8 ft each (12 ft with a driveway), rear 25 ft, building coverage 35%, impervious cover 80%, 35 ft. Two parking spaces per dwelling unit, four in all, behind the building line and with hard surfaces
value.note: The house becomes a two-family dwelling, so it is not a unit added to a single-family house. On a lot in the floodplain the Chapter 8 rules also apply

value.name: Two-family attached dwelling (A)
value.conditions: Two-family dwellings attached in a group of at most six. 3,000 sq ft per dwelling unit and 6,000 sq ft per two-family dwelling, 20 ft wide, rear yard 20 ft, building coverage 30%, 35 ft. Two parking spaces per dwelling unit
value.note: The A district permits no single-family dwelling

historic_bypass.note: No historic district or historic path was found in Chapter 27

districts_read_no_listing.note: None lists a second unit on a single-family lot. R-B and R-C permit two-family detached dwellings and A two-family attached dwellings (see the other paths). C-1, C, LI, M and REC permit no single-family dwelling

value.condition: In R-D 'No permanent additions or enclosed porches are permitted', 'No accessory buildings are permitted' and 'No business or accessory use is permitted'. An addition or a unit in another building is barred there.
'In residential districts, only one principal building may be erected on each lot.' A separate house on the lot would be a second principal building.

In a floodway no new construction, substantial improvement or other development unless an engineering analysis shows no rise in flood levels, and no new construction without a permit from DEP's regional office. New construction and substantial improvement elsewhere in the floodplain need the lowest floor at or above the regulatory flood elevation, and basements are prohibited. Work on an existing building of 50% or more of its market value is a substantial improvement. Smaller work is elevated or floodproofed to the greatest extent possible.

In an AE area without a floodway, 'No new construction or development shall be located within the area measured 50 feet landward from the top-of-bank of any watercourse' unless DEP's regional office issues the appropriate permit. Development includes the renovation, expansion or alteration of a building, so this reaches work inside the house too.
An accessory structure in the floodplain 'shall not be designed or used for human habitation' and may be at most 200 sq ft. The rule reaches every accessory structure there, elevated or not.

types_allowed.note: No ADU use. A second unit is only possible as a two-family dwelling where one is listed, which in R-B and R-C may be made by altering a detached house

spaces_required.note: No ADU use. 'One- and two-family dwellings: two spaces per dwelling unit'

fraction_rounding.note: 'If the computation results in a fraction, a parking space shall be required for each fractional amount.'

min_lot_sqft.note: Single-family detached dwelling. Lot width at the building line 50 ft, frontage 20 ft. The impervious coverage line of the table is blank

setback_front_ft.note: '30 feet from the street line on each street on which the lot abuts'

setback_side_ft.note: '2 side yards are required with an aggregate of 20 feet, neither of which may be less than 8 feet. A side yard containing a parking space or driveway must be at least 12 feet wide'

min_lot_sqft.note: A single-family detached dwelling in R-B must conform with the R-A regulations (27-501.1), so the R-A figures apply. 50 ft wide

setback_side_ft.note: '2 side yards are required with an aggregate of 20 feet, neither of which may be less than 8 feet. A side yard containing a parking space or driveway must be at least 12 feet wide'

setback_side_ft_by_type.note: The one side yard of a semidetached dwelling

min_lot_sqft.note: R-C permits the R-B uses, which must conform with the R-B regulations, and an R-A use in R-B conforms with the R-A regulations (27-601.1, 27-501.1). So a single-family detached dwelling takes the R-A figures

setback_side_ft.note: '2 side yards are required with an aggregate of 20 feet, neither of which may be less than 8 feet. A side yard containing a parking space or driveway must be at least 12 feet wide'
